caption:
This morning I covered ChatGPT Wallet: AI agents can now pay, with a security check on every purchase.

Three new data points. Entry price is $100 a month for ChatGPT Pro, against $20 for Claude Duet. Visa's test of 22 AI models as shoppers found a 42.8% failure rate. The earlier Instant Checkout reached only about 30 Shopify merchants.

My take: approval is the easy part. Measure how often the agent fails and converts before you hand it a card.

Comment SDR and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet this morning: agents can pay, with a security check on every purchase. I went back in to check the numbers around it.
First, getting in costs money. Dots need ChatGPT Pro, priced from $100 a month, against $20 for Anthropic's Claude Duet agent.
Second, Visa tested 22 AI models as shoppers and they failed 42.8% of the time. That is agents in general, not Wallet.
Third, the predecessor, Instant Checkout, reached only about 30 Shopify merchants before OpenAI dropped it. Reach was the problem last time.
My take: approval is the easy part. Before giving an agent a card, measure how often it fails and how often it converts.
